amendments.consequence: Offline adjudication becomes the primary defence, not the quiet machine: the 0xDEADBEEF poison, both sentinels and the full 16-GPR dump decide whether a dispatch really ran, per EXP-0160's evidence-validity filter (two agreeing clean dumps win outright -- contamination can destroy an observation but never fabricate a coherent one). harness/procsample.py records what was ACTUALLY running for the duration into raw/<run>/03_procsample.jsonl, so concurrency is a measurement rather than an assumption, and a contaminated stretch can be located by timestamp against sweep.jsonl's own `t`.
amendments.touches: WHEN the runs execute, and which anti-contamination instrument is primary. Nothing in program construction, splicing, poisoning, majority-of-3, victim classification, the sentinels, the oracles, outcome classification, the coverage rule or the promotion gate changes.
amendments.what: Both gated runs execute UNLOCKED and CONCURRENTLY with sibling experiments. PRE_REGISTRATION section 5 said they would run in an orchestrator-coordinated quiet window; that is superseded for every arm except DSTORE.
amendments.why: Orchestrator ruling 2026-08-30. FIELD-SWEEP-PROTOCOL section 7 is the standing directive -- ordinary sweeps run unlocked; only CONFIRMATION passes need a quiet machine -- and serializing costs far more than the contamination does. EXP-0168, EXP-0171 and EXP-0172 run alongside.

amendments.touches: which fields get a VERDICT. Every field is still swept; only the ruling is withheld. Device field count unchanged at 57.
amendments.what: `get_sr.dst_hi` CONFIRMED in this experiment's verdict scope. `get_sr.form` moved OUT: it belongs to EXP-0172 (a 'one-field-away' row). FOREIGN_FIELDS becomes per-descriptor: {'dst' (any descriptor, EXP-0168), 'get_sr.form' (EXP-0172)}.
amendments.why: Orchestrator ruling 2026-08-30: EXP-0168 owns the field NAME `dst` exactly; `dst_hi` is a different name and a different bit span. get_sr is therefore touched by three experiments on DISJOINT fields.

amendments.touches: run scheduling and analysis pairing. analysis/verdicts.py now accepts N run directories and, PER FIELD, uses the two runs that reached the most distinct attributed values -- EXP-0164 cross_run's own rule -- so the DSTORE pair is not diluted by pair 1. No case, encoding, oracle or gate changes.
amendments.what: TWO gated pairs instead of one. Pair 1 = g17p_20260830_run01 / run02, every arm EXCEPT DSTORE. Pair 2 = g17p_20260830_run03 / run04, DSTORE ONLY, run LAST, after pair 1's raw has been pulled back, and only after telling the orchestrator so the other agents are held off the machine for its duration.
amendments.why: Orchestrator ruling 2026-08-30. The DSTORE arm sweeps device_store.base_slot 0..255, i.e. stores through UNBOUND binding slots -- exactly the hang-prone case FIELD-SWEEP-PROTOCOL section 7 carves out of the run-unlocked rule. Running it last means a wedge costs one arm, not the experiment.

amendments.touches: analysis output only. No device behaviour, no gate, no case.
amendments.what: analysis/recitation.py now also reports, per citation-recoverable field, the fraction of the field's ENCODABLE RANGE the passing arm actually dispatched.
amendments.why: Self-falsification of this experiment's own headline offline finding. EXP-0164's gate (stable_live) has NO coverage term -- THIN_COMMON=8 exists in audit.py but only sets an informational `thin_cross_run` flag and is never consulted by stable_live. So `RECOVERABLE-BY-CITATION` means 'clears EXP-0164's gate', NOT 'meets the docs/evidence-classification.md section 2 hardware-run RANGE bar'. Only 4 of the 12 clear it over the full encodable range; the other 8 clear it on as little as 2 of 64 values. Reporting the 12 without that column would have overstated them.

amendments.touches: the contract's own hash table. No case, encoding, carrier, oracle, poison, sentinel, ladder, coverage rule or promotion gate changes; the three .metal kernels and every other harness blob hash UNCHANGED.
amendments.what: Four entries of authored_sha256 are corrected to the hashes of the files that actually exist: analysis/recitation.py, analysis/verdicts.py, harness/run.py, harness/selftest.py. The stale-and-actual pairs are recorded verbatim in `stale_hashes_corrected` below so the discrepancy is auditable rather than erased.
amendments.why: HONEST DISCLOSURE, found on resume. The M5 progress entry claims the contract was re-frozen over 18 blobs after the amendment_03/amendment_04 edits; it was not, for these four files. A session-limit kill landed between editing them and recomputing their hashes. The four hashes the contract named match NO git object -- they were an in-session version that was never committed -- so the named versions are unrecoverable and cannot be restored. The current files were verified to contain exactly the amendment-authorized changes and nothing else: recitation.py carries the amendment_04 coverage columns, verdicts.py carries the amendment_03 N-run per-field pairing, and harness/selftest.py still reports 0 failures.
amendments.why_this_is_not_a_post_hoc_repair: The freeze exists to stop the harness being edited AFTER data is seen. At the moment of this correction raw/ contains exactly one file, its own README.md: ZERO device dispatches have occurred in this experiment, so no observation exists that these edits could have been fitted to. Had any capture existed, the correct action would have been a new experiment number, not this amendment.

amendments.authority: the PINNED snapshot, not live repo state. tools/agx-isa/db.json has itself already drifted on to 1062 fields under EXP-0165's concurrent edits; pinning is what makes this experiment reproducible.
amendments.not_touched: the neo's shared ~/agxre/tools/ is left exactly as it was: EXP-0168, EXP-0171 and EXP-0172 are sweeping against it concurrently and mutating it under them would be a courtesy violation of FIELD-SWEEP-PROTOCOL 7.
amendments.touches: which db.json the hardware and the analysis are keyed to. No case, encoding, carrier, oracle, ladder, coverage rule or promotion gate changes.
amendments.verified: assemble/disassemble round-trip on falu2 and imm_encode/imm_decode against the pinned pair; harness/selftest.py still 0 failures; and anchors.py run on G17P BEFORE and AFTER the fix produced BYTE-IDENTICAL anchor_report.json and arm_resolution.json -- the difference is a field partition over the same bits, not a length rule, so no observation was affected. Both stale artefacts are retained: work/anchors_staledb_20260830/, work/frozen_neo_stale_20260830/.
amendments.what: work/frozen/ is populated from the PINNED work/db.snapshot.json plus tools/agx-isa/isadb.py, and that pair is pushed to the neo at ~/agxre/EXP-0169/work/frozen/ so isa_helpers._find_isadb() resolves to it on BOTH sides. pinned_inputs_sha256 gains work/frozen/db.json and work/frozen/isadb.py.
amendments.why: The neo's shared ~/agxre/tools/agx-isa/db.json is STALE: 1036 fields / 171 instructions against the pinned snapshot's 1060 / 172, with 65 field geometries differing -- three of them on falu2, this experiment's wave A primary descriptor. The stale copy predates EXP-0138's split of bits 40..42 into srcA_class (40,1) + srcB_class (41,2) and instead carries a single mod_lo (40,3). work/frozen did not exist on the neo, so _find_isadb() fell through to that stale copy. H4(a) tests EXP-0138's model AT srcB_class==1, a field name absent from the stale db, so raw_schema.field_is_a_db_field_name would have been violated and verdicts.field_geometry() would have keyed every falu2 verdict to mod_lo -- silently dropping two in-scope fields and inventing one out-of-scope field.
